title: Fair Credit Reporting Act
summary: Governs the accuracy, fairness, and privacy of information in consumer credit reports. Gives consumers the right to access their files, dispute inaccurate items, and be notified when reports are used against them.
key_provisions: Consumers may dispute inaccurate information; reporting agencies must investigate within 30 days
One free credit report per year from each nationwide agency
Adverse action notice required when a report is used to deny credit, employment, or insurance
Permissible-purpose limits on who may pull a report

title: Truth in Lending Act
summary: Requires clear, uniform disclosure of the cost of credit so consumers can compare terms. Standardizes how the annual percentage rate and finance charges are presented.
key_provisions: APR and total finance charge must be disclosed before consummation
Right of rescission within 3 business days on certain home-secured loans
Periodic statement and billing-error resolution requirements
Ability-to-repay determination for mortgage originations

title: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act
summary: Prohibits abusive, deceptive, and unfair practices by third-party debt collectors and sets rules for how and when they may contact consumers.
key_provisions: Validation notice required within 5 days of initial communication
Consumer may demand verification of the debt and dispute it
Consumer may require the collector to cease communication
Bans harassment, false representations, and contact at inconvenient times

title: Equal Credit Opportunity Act
summary: Prohibits discrimination in any aspect of a credit transaction on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance.
key_provisions: Adverse action notice with specific reasons required within 30 days
Prohibits discouraging applicants on a prohibited basis
Spousal-signature and income-source restrictions
Record retention of applications for 25 months

title: Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act
summary: Governs the mortgage settlement process and servicing. Aims to eliminate kickbacks and ensure borrowers receive timely disclosures of settlement costs and servicing practices.
key_provisions: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure timing requirements
Prohibition on kickbacks and unearned fees for referrals
Servicer must acknowledge and resolve qualified written requests / error notices
Escrow account limits and annual analysis

title: Electronic Fund Transfer Act
summary: Establishes the rights and liabilities of consumers using electronic fund transfers — debit cards, ATMs, ACH, and prepaid accounts — including error-resolution and limited liability for unauthorized transfers.
key_provisions: Error-resolution investigation within 10 business days (45 with provisional credit)
Tiered liability caps for unauthorized transfers reported promptly
Disclosure of terms before the first EFT
Receipts and periodic statements for electronic transfers

title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
summary: Requires financial institutions to explain their information-sharing practices and to safeguard sensitive consumer data.
key_provisions: Annual privacy notice describing data-sharing practices
Right to opt out of sharing with non-affiliated third parties
Safeguards Rule requiring an information-security program
Pretexting protections against obtaining information under false pretenses

title: Dodd-Frank UDAAP Authority
implementing_regulation: Consumer Financial Protection Act (Title X of Dodd-Frank)
summary: Prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices by providers of consumer financial products and services. The CFPB's broadest enforcement hook, applicable across product lines.
key_provisions: Unfair: causes substantial injury not reasonably avoidable and not outweighed by benefits
Deceptive: misleads a reasonable consumer to their detriment
Abusive: materially interferes with understanding or exploits a lack of understanding
Applies regardless of whether a product-specific rule was also violated

title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act
summary: Provides financial and legal protections to active-duty servicemembers, including interest-rate caps and foreclosure / repossession protections.
key_provisions: 6% interest-rate cap on pre-service obligations during active duty
Protection against default judgments
Foreclosure protections without a court order
Right to terminate certain leases on deployment

title: Home Mortgage Disclosure Act
summary: Requires many lenders to collect and publicly report mortgage application data, used to detect discriminatory lending patterns and assess whether institutions serve community housing needs.
key_provisions: Collection of loan-level application data (LAR)
Public disclosure of mortgage lending data
Used by regulators to screen for redlining and fair-lending issues

title: Truth in Savings Act
summary: Requires depository institutions to disclose fees, the annual percentage yield, interest rates, and other terms for deposit accounts so consumers can compare savings products.
key_provisions: Uniform APY disclosure for comparison shopping
Fee schedule disclosure before account opening
Advance notice of adverse changes to account terms
Rules on how balances are calculated for interest

title: Fair Credit Billing Act
implementing_regulation: Regulation Z (12 CFR Part 1026, Subpart B)
summary: An amendment to TILA that addresses billing-error disputes on open-end credit such as credit cards, giving consumers a process to challenge incorrect charges.
key_provisions: Consumer may dispute a billing error in writing within 60 days
Creditor must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve within two billing cycles
Charge in dispute may be withheld during investigation
Protections for unauthorized charges and goods not delivered

title: Consumer Leasing Act
summary: Requires clear disclosure of the costs and terms of consumer leases of personal property, such as vehicle leases, and limits balloon payments.
key_provisions: Disclosure of total lease cost, payments, and fees before signing
Limits on residual-value balloon liability at lease end
Standardized advertising rules for lease terms

title: Military Lending Act
summary: Caps the cost of consumer credit extended to active-duty servicemembers and their dependents and bans certain abusive loan features.
key_provisions: 36% Military Annual Percentage Rate (MAPR) cap, including most fees
Bans mandatory arbitration and prepayment penalties for covered borrowers
Requires a covered-borrower check and specific MAPR disclosures

title: Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act
summary: A 2003 amendment to FCRA focused on identity-theft prevention, fraud alerts, and free annual credit reports.
key_provisions: Free annual credit report from each nationwide agency (AnnualCreditReport.com)
Fraud alerts and credit freezes for identity-theft victims
Truncation of card numbers on receipts and identity-theft blocking of disputed items

title: Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act
summary: A TILA amendment imposing extra protections on high-cost mortgages, targeting predatory home-equity lending.
key_provisions: Triggers extra disclosures and protections when rate/fee thresholds are exceeded
Bans balloon payments, negative amortization, and certain prepayment penalties on covered loans
Requires homeownership counseling before a high-cost loan

title: Credit Card Accountability Responsibility and Disclosure Act
summary: The 2009 CARD Act curbs surprise credit-card fees and rate hikes and adds protections for consumers under 21.
key_provisions: 45-day advance notice of rate increases; limits on retroactive rate hikes
Payments above the minimum applied to the highest-APR balance first
Ability-to-pay underwriting and limits on fees for consumers under 21

title: Expedited Funds Availability Act
summary: Sets maximum hold periods for deposited funds so consumers know when checks and deposits become available.
key_provisions: Next-day availability for cash and certain low-risk deposits
Maximum hold schedules for local and exception holds
Disclosure of the institution's funds-availability policy

title: Check Clearing for the 21st Century Act
summary: Enables banks to process digital images of checks (substitute checks), speeding collection and clearing.
key_provisions: Legal equivalence of a properly prepared substitute check to the original
Expedited recredit rights when a substitute check causes a loss
Consumer disclosures about substitute checks

title: Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act
summary: Gives electronic signatures and records the same legal effect as paper, provided consumers consent to electronic disclosures.
key_provisions: Electronic records satisfy 'in writing' requirements when consumers consent
Consumer must affirmatively consent and be able to access the electronic format
Record-retention rules for electronically signed agreements

title: S.A.F.E. Mortgage Licensing Act
implementing_regulation: Regulations G and H (12 CFR Parts 1007, 1008)
summary: Requires mortgage loan originators to register or be licensed and listed in the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System (NMLS).
key_provisions: Unique NMLS identifier for every mortgage loan originator
Registration (depository) or state licensing (non-depository) requirement
Background checks and continuing-education standards

title: Mortgage Assistance Relief Services Rule
summary: Protects homeowners from foreclosure-rescue and loan-modification scams by banning advance fees and deceptive claims.
key_provisions: Bans collection of any fee until the consumer accepts a written offer from their servicer
Prohibits advising consumers to stop communicating with their lender
Mandatory disclosures that the provider is not affiliated with the government or lender

title: Mortgage Acts and Practices – Advertising Rule
summary: Prohibits deceptive claims in advertising for mortgage products and credit.
key_provisions: Bans misrepresentations about rates, payments, fees, and government affiliation
Applies to any commercial communication about mortgage credit
Record-keeping of advertisements for 24 months

title: Homeowners Protection Act
summary: Governs private mortgage insurance (PMI), requiring automatic termination and consumer-requested cancellation at defined equity levels.
key_provisions: Automatic PMI termination at 78% loan-to-value
Borrower right to request cancellation at 80% LTV
Annual disclosure of PMI cancellation rights

title: Fair Housing Act
summary: Prohibits discrimination in residential real-estate transactions, including mortgage lending, complementing ECOA.
key_provisions: Bans discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, or national origin
Covers mortgage lending, appraisals, and homeowners insurance
Prohibits redlining and discriminatory terms

title: Remittance Transfer Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation E, Subpart B (12 CFR Part 1005.30)
summary: Extends EFTA protections to international money transfers, requiring upfront disclosures and error-resolution rights.
key_provisions: Pre-payment disclosure of exchange rate, fees, and amount to be received
30-minute cancellation window for most transfers
Error-resolution and refund rights for failed or incorrect transfers

title: Prepaid Accounts Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulations E and Z (12 CFR Parts 1005, 1026)
summary: Extends consumer protections to prepaid accounts, including standardized fee disclosures and fraud protection.
key_provisions: Short-form and long-form fee disclosures before acquisition
Error-resolution and limited liability for registered accounts
Credit-feature protections aligned with credit-card rules

title: Debt Collection Rule
summary: The CFPB's 2021 rule implementing the FDCPA, modernizing limits on collector contact frequency and electronic communications.
key_provisions: Presumptive limit of seven calls per debt within seven days
Rules for email/text contact and an opt-out mechanism
Validation-notice content and time-barred-debt disclosure requirements

title: Payday, Vehicle Title, and High-Cost Installment Loan Rule
summary: Regulates short-term and high-cost loans, focused on preventing repeated unsuccessful withdrawal attempts from borrower accounts.
key_provisions: Bans further withdrawal attempts after two consecutive failures without new authorization
Notice requirements before attempting account withdrawals
Record-keeping and compliance-program obligations

title: Mortgage Servicing Rules
summary: Sets servicer obligations for periodic statements, error resolution, and loss-mitigation handling.
key_provisions: Loss-mitigation evaluation procedures and dual-tracking limits
Periodic statements and prompt payment crediting
Timely response to notices of error and information requests

title: TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure Rule
summary: The 'Know Before You Owe' rule merging TILA and RESPA mortgage disclosures into the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure.
key_provisions: Loan Estimate within 3 business days of application
Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing
Tolerance limits on how much certain fees may increase

title: Ability-to-Repay / Qualified Mortgage Rule
summary: Requires lenders to make a reasonable, good-faith determination that a borrower can repay a mortgage.
key_provisions: Verification of income, assets, debts, and obligations before origination
Qualified Mortgage safe harbor for loans meeting defined standards
Limits on risky features like interest-only and negative amortization for QMs

title: Loan Originator Compensation Rule
summary: Bans compensating mortgage loan originators based on loan terms, to curb steering into costlier loans.
key_provisions: Originator pay may not vary with the interest rate or other loan terms
Anti-steering safe harbor requiring options to be presented
Qualification and identification requirements for originators

title: Debit Card Interchange and Routing (Durbin Amendment)
summary: Caps debit-card interchange fees for large issuers and requires multiple network-routing options for merchants.
key_provisions: Interchange fee standard for issuers above the asset threshold
At least two unaffiliated networks must be available for routing
Bans network exclusivity and routing restrictions

title: Telephone Consumer Protection Act
summary: Restricts autodialed calls and texts, frequently invoked against debt collectors contacting consumers' cell phones.
key_provisions: Prior express consent required for autodialed or prerecorded calls to cell phones
Revocation of consent must be honored
Statutory damages per violating call or text

title: Bank Secrecy Act
summary: Anti-money-laundering law requiring institutions to monitor and report suspicious activity; often the reason behind account freezes or closures.
key_provisions: Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs)
Risk-based AML program and monitoring requirements
Recordkeeping for funds transfers and account activity

title: Customer Identification Program (USA PATRIOT Act §326)
summary: Requires institutions to verify customer identity when opening accounts, the 'Know Your Customer' baseline.
key_provisions: Collect and verify name, date of birth, address, and identification number
Maintain records of the information used to verify identity
Check customers against government watchlists

title: Right to Financial Privacy Act
summary: Limits federal government access to consumers' financial records held by institutions, requiring notice or legal process.
key_provisions: Government generally must provide notice and an opportunity to object
Requires a subpoena, summons, or warrant for record access
Recordkeeping of disclosures to government authorities

title: FTC Act Section 5 (Unfair or Deceptive Acts)
summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce; the FTC's general authority over non-bank financial actors.
key_provisions: Deception: a material representation likely to mislead a reasonable consumer
Unfairness: substantial, unavoidable injury not outweighed by benefits
Basis for many FTC consumer-finance enforcement actions

title: Credit Repair Organizations Act
implementing_regulation: Enforced by the CFPB and FTC
summary: Regulates credit-repair companies, banning advance fees and false claims about improving credit.
key_provisions: No payment until promised services are fully performed
Written contract with a 3-day cancellation right
Bans misrepresenting what the organization can do for a consumer's credit

title: FTC Holder in Due Course Rule
summary: Preserves a consumer's right to raise seller-related claims and defenses against any holder of the credit contract.
key_provisions: Required notice making assignees subject to the borrower's claims against the seller
Protects buyers when goods are defective or undelivered
Recovery limited to amounts already paid under the contract

title: FTC Credit Practices Rule
summary: Bans certain unfair provisions in consumer credit contracts and requires a cosigner notice.
key_provisions: Prohibits confessions of judgment and certain wage-assignment clauses
Bans non-purchase-money security interests in household goods
Requires a clear written notice to cosigners of their liability

title: Identity Theft Red Flags Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation V (12 CFR Part 1022, Subpart J)
summary: Requires institutions with covered accounts to maintain a program to detect and respond to identity-theft warning signs.
key_provisions: Written Identity Theft Prevention Program
Detection of 'red flags' indicating possible identity theft
Procedures to respond to and update for new threats

title: Risk-Based Pricing Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation V (12 CFR Part 1022, Subpart H)
summary: Requires a notice when a consumer receives credit on materially worse terms based on a credit report.
key_provisions: Risk-based pricing notice when worse terms result from report information
Credit-score-disclosure exception notices as an alternative
Lets consumers learn that their report affected their terms

title: FCRA Disposal Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation V (16 CFR Part 682 / 12 CFR Part 1022)
summary: Requires proper disposal of consumer-report information to prevent unauthorized access and identity theft.
key_provisions: Reasonable measures to dispose of consumer-report data
Covers paper shredding and secure electronic destruction
Applies to anyone who maintains consumer-report information

title: FCRA Affiliate Marketing Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation V (12 CFR Part 1022, Subpart C)
summary: Gives consumers the right to opt out of affiliates using shared information to market to them.
key_provisions: Opt-out notice before affiliates use shared eligibility information for marketing
Opt-out effective for at least five years
Clear and conspicuous disclosure requirements

title: FCRA Furnisher Accuracy and Dispute Rule
implementing_regulation: Regulation V (12 CFR Part 1022, Subpart E)
summary: Sets accuracy and dispute-investigation duties for companies that furnish account data to credit bureaus.
key_provisions: Duty to furnish accurate information and correct known errors
Investigate direct and indirect (bureau-routed) disputes
Reasonable written policies to ensure data accuracy and integrity

title: Higher Education Act
summary: Governs federal student-aid programs, including servicing standards, income-driven repayment, and borrower-defense discharge.
key_provisions: Income-driven repayment and loan-consolidation options
Borrower-defense and closed-school discharge rights
Servicing and disclosure standards for federal loans

title: Flood Disaster Protection Act
summary: Requires flood insurance on mortgaged property in special flood-hazard areas and governs lender escrow and notice duties.
key_provisions: Mandatory flood insurance for loans secured by property in flood zones
Notice to borrowers of flood-hazard status
Escrow of flood-insurance premiums and force-placement rules

title: Alternative Mortgage Transaction Parity Act
summary: Permits state-chartered lenders to offer adjustable-rate and other alternative mortgages under federal parity standards.
key_provisions: Parity for variable-rate and balloon mortgage structures
Applies CFPB disclosure standards to covered alternative mortgages
Limits which federal rules preempt state restrictions

title: Garnishment of Federal Benefit Payments Rule
summary: Protects exempt federal benefit deposits (e.g., Social Security) from being frozen or garnished by creditors.
key_provisions: Banks must perform a lookback to protect recent federal-benefit deposits
Protected amount must remain accessible despite a garnishment order
Notice to the account holder when a garnishment is received

title: Regulation E Overdraft Opt-In Rule
summary: Requires consumers to affirmatively opt in before a bank may charge overdraft fees on ATM and one-time debit transactions.
key_provisions: No overdraft fees on ATM/one-time debit without prior opt-in
Standardized opt-in disclosure describing the service and fees
Right to revoke the opt-in at any time

title: Consumer Financial Protection Act (Dodd-Frank Title X)
summary: Established the CFPB and its supervisory, rulemaking, and enforcement authority over consumer financial products and services.
key_provisions: Defines covered persons and service providers under CFPB jurisdiction
Authority to supervise banks and larger nonbank participants
Foundation for the CFPB's UDAAP and rulemaking power

title: GLBA Safeguards Rule
summary: Requires financial institutions to develop and maintain an information-security program protecting customer data.
key_provisions: Written information-security program with a qualified individual in charge
Risk assessment, access controls, and encryption of customer data
Incident-response plan and vendor-oversight requirements

title: Private Education Loan Disclosures (TILA)
summary: Sets special disclosure and timing rules for private student loans, distinct from federal student aid.
key_provisions: Application, approval, and final disclosures at defined stages
30-day acceptance window and 3-day right to cancel before disbursement
Self-certification form confirming cost of attendance

title: Regulation D (Reserve Requirements / Savings Transfers)
implementing_regulation: Regulation D (12 CFR Part 204, Federal Reserve)
summary: Defines deposit-account categories; historically limited certain convenient transfers from savings accounts to six per month.
key_provisions: Distinguishes transaction accounts from savings deposits
Historic six-per-month limit on certain savings transfers (suspended in 2020)
Underlies fees and restrictions some banks still apply to savings

title: OFAC Economic Sanctions
summary: Requires institutions to block or reject transactions involving sanctioned parties or countries; a common reason for held or returned transfers.
key_provisions: Screening against the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list
Blocking or rejecting prohibited transactions
Mandatory reporting of blocked and rejected transactions

title: Gift Card Rules (CARD Act)
summary: Protects holders of gift cards and certain prepaid cards from short expiration dates and surprise dormancy fees.
key_provisions: Funds may not expire for at least five years from the date loaded
Limits on dormancy and inactivity fees, with disclosure
Clear disclosure of fees and expiration on the card or packaging

title: CARES Act Credit Reporting Protections
summary: Requires furnishers that grant a pandemic-related accommodation to report the account as current if the consumer meets the terms.
key_provisions: Accounts under an accommodation reported as current if not already delinquent
Applies to forbearance and modified-payment arrangements
Protects credit standing during qualifying hardships

title: Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act
summary: Protects bona fide tenants in foreclosed properties by giving them notice and time before eviction.
key_provisions: Bona fide leases generally survive foreclosure
At least 90 days' notice to vacate for tenants
Successor owner takes title subject to the existing tenancy

title: Appraisal Independence Requirements
summary: Protects the independence of mortgage appraisers and requires consumers receive copies of valuations.
key_provisions: Bans coercion or pressure to influence an appraiser's valuation
Requires copies of appraisals be provided to applicants
Customary-and-reasonable compensation for fee appraisers

title: Medical Debt Credit Reporting Rule
summary: CFPB rule restricting the inclusion and use of medical debt information in consumer credit reports and lending decisions.
key_provisions: Limits reporting of covered medical debts on consumer reports
Restricts creditor reliance on medical-debt information
Aims to reduce errors and coercive medical-billing collection

title: Higher-Priced Mortgage Loan Escrow Rule
summary: Requires escrow accounts and an appraisal for higher-priced (subprime-range) mortgage loans.
key_provisions: Mandatory escrow for taxes and insurance for a minimum period
Written appraisal with physical inspection for covered loans
Additional appraisal for certain quick 'flipped' resales

title: FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule
summary: Regulates telemarketing, including debt-relief services, with an advance-fee ban for debt settlement.
key_provisions: No advance fees for debt-relief services until a debt is settled
Mandatory disclosures and bans on misrepresentations
Do-Not-Call and calling-time restrictions

title: Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act
summary: Requires disclosures in the interstate sale of subdivided land to protect buyers from fraud.
key_provisions: Property Report disclosure before a purchase agreement is signed
Buyer rescission rights within defined periods
Anti-fraud provisions for covered land sales

title: Credit Card Penalty Fees Rule
summary: CFPB rule limiting the safe-harbor amount large card issuers may charge for late payments.
key_provisions: Lower safe-harbor late-fee amount for larger card issuers
Late fees must be reasonable and proportional to costs
Issuers may exceed the safe harbor only with a cost-justification analysis
